clue.text: A number with shared fear, we hear, about savage nomad

indicators.note: about means going round, so the first part is wrapped round the nomad
we hear tells the solver that the phrase is to be taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: people with a shared fear have one dread between them
a Hun was one of the savage nomadic people who overran Europe

explanation.surface: Someone describes a group united in terror of a barbarian wanderer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' covers only the shared fear (one dread, said aloud); the savage nomad is wrapped inside it, splitting the figure as one-Hun-dred.
explanation.definitionFit: A hundred is a cardinal figure, a count of ten tens.

clue.text: Sickness, not half, has a Greek shepherd going back to find Phaeacian princess

indicators.note: not half asks for only the first half of the word for sickness, dropping its last three letters

parts.note: nausea is sickness

indicators.note: going back means the article and the shepherd are read backwards together

parts.note: Acis is the shepherd loved by Galatea in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A queasy traveller and a herdsman retreat to discover a royal girl from Homer's island.
explanation.walkthrough: Acis, Galatea's lover, is Sicilian in most tellings; 'going back' turns the article and his name together, not one at a time.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Odyssey the daughter of King Alcinous of Phaeacia finds the shipwrecked Odysseus on the shore.

clue.text: Where we discretely abandoned a version of She

indicators.note: discretely means separately, so the two letters are dropped one by one from the word where

parts.note: the letters W and E, taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about where a variant of Haggard's novel was left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: W and E are not side by side in WHERE, hence 'discretely' (separately): removing them leaves the pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: The object-case pronoun is the form 'She' takes after a verb or preposition.

clue.text: One I notice at source of Nile?

definitions.text: One I notice at source of Nile?

indicators.note: source of picks the opening letter of the river's name

parts.note: A means one
an ad is a notice in a paper

explanation.surface: Someone spots a figure at the head of the great African river.
explanation.definitionFit: A water nymph of Greek myth lives in springs and rivers, so one might be found at a river's source.

clue.text: French physicist, note, mural mostly represented holding uranium

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: holding means the reworked letters go round the element's symbol
represented signals that the shortened word is presented in a new order
mostly means all but the last letter of the word mural

parts.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A French scientist is depicted in a wall painting that contains a radioactive element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims the wall painting by its last letter before 'represented' rearranges it; the scale is named after the French scientist, with an accent on the first E.
explanation.definitionFit: René Réaumur devised the temperature scale named after him.

clue.text: Author of The Tents of Wickedness nursing illiberal extremes produces impieties

indicators.note: nursing means holding inside, so the author's name cradles the two letters

parts.words: Author of The Tents of Wickedness
parts.note: Peter De Vries, American comic novelist, wrote The Tents of Wickedness

indicators.note: extremes asks for the first and last letters of the word illiberal

explanation.surface: A novelist's work tolerating narrow-minded ends turns out irreverent acts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Tents of Wickedness' sounds like a book title to define, but it identifies the author, whose surname is cut open by the two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Devilries are wicked or profane deeds, acts of irreverence.

clue.text: Romanian musician renders opera softly rather than one loudly at first

indicators.note: rather than says one letter is put in place of another: P for softly instead of the L that opens loudly

parts.note: Lulu is Berg's opera

explanation.surface: A pianist from Bucharest performs an opera gently instead of at full volume.
explanation.walkthrough: P (piano, softly) replaces an L, the first letter of 'loudly', in LULU.
explanation.definitionFit: Radu Lupu was a celebrated Romanian concert pianist.

clue.text: People like Kijé are still socially acceptable occupants

parts.note: to lie is to stay still
U means upper-class, hence socially acceptable
tenants are occupants of a property

explanation.surface: Fictional officers are said to remain respectable residents.
explanation.walkthrough: Lieutenant Kijé is the imaginary officer of Prokofiev's film score.
explanation.definitionFit: Kijé holds the rank of a junior army officer, so others of his rank are his kind.

clue.text: Playwright depicting irrational Emperor

parts.note: pi is an irrational number
Nero was a Roman emperor

explanation.surface: A dramatist portrays a mad ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Wing Pinero wrote Victorian stage comedies such as The Magistrate.

clue.text: Which was endlessly cueing rage when destroyed

definitions.text: Which was endlessly cueing rage when destroyed

indicators.note: destroyed signals the remaining letters are broken up and rearranged
endlessly removes the last letter of each of the two words cueing and rage

explanation.surface: Something that prompted fury as it was wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' leaves CUEIN and RAG, which 'when destroyed' rearranges. The bombed Basque town, painted by Picasso, still stirs outrage.
explanation.definitionFit: The town bombed in 1937 became, through Picasso's painting, an emblem of wartime fury.

clue.text: Struggle with directions to a city of two music schools

parts.note: to vie is to struggle or compete
N for north, twice, as two compass directions

explanation.surface: A contest with sat-nav guidance to a conservatoire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Vienna is famous for its First and Second Viennese Schools of composers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Austrian capital gave its name to the classical and the twentieth-century Viennese schools.

clue.text: Recorded mass in F; I conducted

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for mass inside the letters around it

parts.note: led means conducted or guided

explanation.surface: A conductor reports taping a Mass in F major.
explanation.definitionFit: To film something is to record it on camera.

clue.text: Beethoven's Opus I shows Angela mostly playing tennis

indicators.note: mostly removes the last letter of the surname of the former German chancellor

parts.note: Angela Merkel was Chancellor of Germany

indicators.note: playing signals the word tennis is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone shows a German politician hitting balls on court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts MERKEL to MERKE; 'playing' rearranges TENNIS to NSTEIN. 'I shows' only links the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Merkenstein is a Beethoven song, published as his Op. 100.

clue.text: I'm back on trial perhaps at end of symphony, Haydn's Opus!

indicators.note: back means the contraction is read in reverse
perhaps signals the word trial is rearranged
at end of picks the final letter of symphony

explanation.surface: A composer's work faces trial again at a symphony's close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns I'M into MI; 'perhaps' rearranges TRIAL to LITAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Haydn's Symphony No. 100 carries the nickname after its martial percussion.

clue.text: Crash car in panic or influenced by a sign

indicators.note: crash signals the letters of the following words are smashed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Smashing your car in a panic, or being guided by a road sign.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'sign' is a sign of the zodiac, not a road sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone born under the zodiac goat is shaped, astrologers say, by that star sign.

clue.text: Sonata (sic) rewritten as Mozart serenade, Köchel No!

indicators.note: rewritten signals the letters of the two words are written out in a new order

explanation.surface: A sonata is redrafted as a Mozart serenade, but the catalogue refuses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No!' adds the legal sense: the word also means annulment of a judgment.
explanation.definitionFit: A cassation is an eighteenth-century outdoor serenade, a genre Mozart wrote in.

clue.text: Photographer, one caught in war in France after start of D-day

indicators.note: caught in means the letter for one is held within the other letters
after means the French word comes after the first letter
start of picks the opening letter of the word for the Normandy landing day

parts.note: guerre is French for war
A means one

explanation.surface: A war photographer is captured in France just after the Normandy landings.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Daguerre invented the daguerreotype, an early photographic process.

clue.text: Holy occasion Dante, say, sure organised

indicators.note: organised signals the letters are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A festival, says Dante, that is surely well planned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dante, say' looks like an example of a poet; his name is simply fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The day of Christ's Resurrection is the holiest feast in the Christian calendar.

clue.text: Enthusiast enthralled by tree-men; Cocteau's were terrible

indicators.note: enthralled by means held captive inside, so the enthusiast sits within the tree-men

parts.note: Ents are Tolkien's tree-men
a fan is an enthusiast

explanation.surface: A devotee is captivated by Tolkien's tree creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: Cocteau's novel is Les Enfants Terribles.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for children completes the title of Cocteau's novel about wild siblings.

clue.text: One inspired by Greek tragedy — Academician with dramatic display for an audience

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician

indicators.note: for an audience means the word is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a scene is a dramatic display, as in making a scene

explanation.surface: A Royal Academy painter makes a theatrical spectacle for the public.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Racine modelled tragedies such as Phèdre on Euripides.

clue.text: Sounds like cascades by a river featuring in opera

indicators.note: by means next to, so the river follows
sounds like means the word is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: falls are cascades of water
the Taff is a river in South Wales

explanation.surface: Waterfalls beside a river feature in an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: The Taff is the river that flows through Cardiff.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's last opera is named after Shakespeare's fat knight.

clue.text: Endless debate that did for Hyacinthus

indicators.note: endless removes the final letter of the word for debate

parts.note: to discuss is to debate

explanation.surface: An unending argument that finished off a mythical youth.
explanation.walkthrough: In myth Apollo killed Hyacinthus by accident with a thrown disc.
explanation.definitionFit: The thrown disc that struck Hyacinthus was what killed him.

clue.text: Rumpelstiltskin, say, beginning to dance over confrontation with female

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of dance

parts.note: war is open confrontation

explanation.surface: The fairy-tale imp starts dancing before squaring up to a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumpelstiltskin is a tiny man of folklore, an example of the little people.

clue.text: Composer, Transylvanian at heart, I understand by start of Introit

indicators.note: at heart picks the middle letter of the thirteen-letter word

parts.note: I get means I understand

indicators.note: start of picks the first letter of Introit

explanation.surface: A composer, Transylvanian at heart, grasps the opening of a church chant.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, the composer was born in Transylvania.
explanation.definitionFit: György Ligeti was a Hungarian composer of works such as Atmosphères.

clue.text: Claypole on island finding rescue vessel

parts.note: Noah Claypole is the bully in Dickens's Oliver Twist
Sark is one of the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: A Dickens character on an island finds a lifeboat.
explanation.definitionFit: The ark saved Noah's family and the animals from the Flood.

clue.text: Which might be used as part of Frenchman's outlay

indicators.note: as part of says the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Something a Frenchman might spend.
explanation.definitionFit: The sou was an old French coin of little value, money to be spent.

clue.text: Sibelius, say, taking a month to frame the central part of Karelia

indicators.note: to frame means to go round, so the month surrounds the middle letter

parts.note: Jan is short for January

indicators.note: the central part of picks the middle letter of Karelia

explanation.surface: The Finnish composer takes a month to depict the heart of a Finnish region.
explanation.definitionFit: Sibelius's first name was Jean, so he is an example of one.

clue.text: Learner often uses reconditioned instruments

indicators.note: reconditioned means rebuilt, so the letters are put together in a new order

parts.note: L stands for learner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: A beginner frequently plays restored instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: These are pipes blown through a nostril, played in Polynesia and elsewhere.
